$Comment: The flagship multi-station fish exemplar, a standalone reusable ACTION attached to Server/RpgStations/Stations/CuttingBoard.json via {"Ref":"PrepFish"}. It is self-contained: every mechanical group it needs is authored here, and a station that Refs it inherits nothing except what it chooses to overlay group-wise. Custody.Input is authored explicitly (ResourceTypeId 'Fish', the native family every caught-fish item shares via Template_Fish_Item.json) because this action has no Recipe for the usual zero-extra-authoring fallback to derive acceptance from - it is a Steps program. Select is deliberately absent, so this action matches any context; the cutting board offers only this one job. Own-asset references are authored PascalCase to match the referenced file's own name (the reserved 'self' anchor aside); matching stays case-insensitive so a casing slip never breaks content. Fish scaling is split into two steps deliberately: 'Load' is a one-shot Consume (Repeat absent) and 'Scale' is a pure Duration beat with no Consume phase (Repeat:{Times:3}) - a Consume inside a Repeat would re-execute the consume every iteration and over-drain custody, so the load and the repeated animation beat are kept separate. Tool gate = the Daggers weapon family, authored onto Tags.Family: vanilla weapons carry native Tags {Type:['Weapon'],Family:['Dagger']} on their shared Template_Weapon_Daggers.json parent, inherited to every material tier at decode time - Tags.Family:['Dagger'] is an any-of match every Daggers tier satisfies with zero per-tier enumeration (a future dagger tier just works, preferring native-category composition over a hand-maintained id list). Anchors.Fire targets the 'CookingFire' station (Server/RpgStations/Stations/CookingFire.json) within a 12-metre radius (MaxRadiusMeters). Work.Looping:true plus the engine's StopReason.INPUTS_EXHAUSTED is 'repeats while fish remain' with zero mode flags - the loop stops gracefully once no more Fish custody remains at the next 'Load' step's Consume. Sound/particle/emote ids are all real, already-shipped-elsewhere ids, never invented placeholders: Smoke_Black (Deco_Campfire_Off.json's own particle), SFX_Player_Drop_Item (the vanilla generic item-place sound), RPG_Emote_Knife (this jar's own Server/Emote/RPG_Emote_Knife.json). Every added id is likewise real and one-shot (never a Looping SoundEvent: nothing in the protocol can stop a playing sound, so a looping id fired through a step Presentation would never end): 'Scale' uses SFX_Daggers_T1_Slash_Impact (the dagger's own blade-lands impact - the knife swing is already carried visually by the RPG_Emote_Knife clip, so the audio beat is the chop landing) plus Block_Hit_Wood chips (the vanilla wood-hit chip+dust system - a knife biting into the wooden board); both re-fire on each of the 3 scale beats, since a step's entry cues run inside the per-iteration loop and a Repeat:{Times:3} step therefore cues three times with zero engine change. 'Cook' authors IsWork:true (a pure Duration beat is not a Consume+Produce convert, so it must opt in explicitly) which is what puts the fire into its Lit state for exactly this beat, plus SFX_Flame_Ignite as the sizzle one-shot at beat entry (Sounds/Items/Torch/Torch_On.ogg - the flare of food meeting hot coals). 'Harvest' gets a deliberately silent steam puff (Block_Break_Dust: a bounded 2-particle Smoke_Cartoon burst rendered BlendAdd, so it reads bright/white and dissipates in about 0.5s) - the one visually-approximate id in this action, since the engine ships no standalone steam/vapor particle system at all (the only vapour in the game is a Vapor_Water spawner nested inside Workbench_Cooking_On, not referenceable as a standalone SystemId). Custody.Display renders the placed fish following the sawmill's own display conventions (Offset/Rotation are facing-relative to the placed block's yaw, so a Y-only offset stays orientation-safe at any block rotation; the sawmill uses Offset.Y -0.1 / Scale 0.4, the cooking fire Offset.Y 0.4 / Scale 1.0). Offset.Y 0.05 (a fish laid just above the board's top face) and Scale 0.5 (a fish item is small next to a log) are provisional - in-game tuning is expected, exactly as the sawmill's own values were tuned in-game. No Worker group is authored here: the walking puppet this program requires is supplied by whichever station attaches the action, which is where placement values belong (a cutting board and a filleting table stand the worker in different places).
Label: rpgstations.action.prepfish.label
